title: Module contract, tool modules and presets
objective: Finish the module contract so a new tool is a declaration plus its equations: declared source kinds, one presettable-action rule, field patches over the whole parameter vocabulary with structural invariants, a descriptor snapshot instead of hand-kept lists, a smaller ToolModule and descriptor, developer-only test modules, and the shared Exposure and White balance controls.
context_summary: The consolidation made Basic, the colour mixer, Presence and the vignette one field-patch module each, gave the host layer identity, format and mask, and one placement rule. Waves 1 to 3 declared each effect's source kinds, put JPEG and RAW photos on one Exposure and White balance control set (RAW's through control variants), resolved whether an action is presettable through one registry method, generalised field patches to the whole parameter vocabulary with a validating Spec builder (the developer controls proof is now a field-patch spec), replaced the hand-kept lists of built-in modules with one committed descriptor snapshot (fixtures/modules/builtin-descriptors.json) and made the vignette's falloff tables lazy. What remains: the trait and the descriptor carry mechanisms with one user (three describe hooks always read together, two history-label mechanisms, a JSON-descriptor parse path no production code calls, builder setters that silently do nothing on the wrong variant); the pixel proof is registered in every build; and per-module tests restate what the conformance suite proves. The owner's decisions are in docs/decisions.md's "Post-consolidation review" section; constraints are in docs/design/post-consolidation.md.

tasks.description: Replace the preset importer's false "Luxforge has no masks" message and correct the presets design doc's stale masking and catalog-format passages.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. Masking is delivered, so telling an importing user Luxforge has no masks is a false statement about current behavior, not a scope note.

`presets/mapping.rs`'s `NO_MASKS` constant reads "Luxforge has no masks or local corrections" and is reported for every imported Lightroom mask row; `presets/tests.rs` asserts that exact text. `docs/design/presets.md` repeats "Luxforge has no such tool" for the same row, and separately says "The current format is 7" with the format's branch history, while the catalog's own format marker is 10.

Reword the reason to something like "Lightroom masks and local corrections are not imported" (mask presets stay out of scope by decision; only the wording is wrong). Point the format passage at its one authoritative home instead of restating the number or its history.
No behavior changes: the importer still refuses Lightroom mask settings, only the message and the doc text change.

tasks.description: Declare each effect's source-kind applicability on EffectDescriptor and resolve "does this apply to this photo" through one function used by action refusal, admission, module.list and the desktop.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. Declared source kinds remove the desktop's name checks in the same change.

The rule "RAW applies only to a RAW photo" is written six times today: `api/methods.rs`'s `module_list` filters the literal `"luxforge.raw"`, but only when the request carries an `asset_id`; the desktop's own call to it (`app/tasks.rs`'s `modules_task`) sends none, so the desktop's own checks are what actually enforce this there. `editor/source.rs`'s `validate_source_recipe` names `crate::RAW_EFFECT` directly on its JPEG branch. tasks.description: Resolve "is this a presettable action" and its settings-set shape through one registry method used by the preset library, capture, apply, the Lightroom mapping and composite plans.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation.

The rule "registered, a `patch: true` action, and its module available" is checked at six sites in three vocabularies: `presets/mod.rs`'s `validate_settings` (238-276); `presets/library.rs`'s `unavailable_actions` (179-189) and `capture_action` (658-682), which adds `check_applies_to(kind)`; `presets/mapping.rs`'s `transfer_value` (1187-1200) and `writable` (1212-1225), worded "Luxforge has no X action" and "X is not available"; and `editor/plan.rs`'s `resolve_plan` (486-494), which checks unknown and patch and reaches availability only later, through `ask()`.

The settings-set shape (1 to 16 valid action names, each a non-empty object of at most 64 fields) is checked twice in two wordings: `modules/descriptor.rs`'s `check_settings` (~2638-2673), the parameter check every settings parameter gets, says "must name 1..=16 actions" and words an empty and an oversized field object separately, while `validate_settings` says "names 1 to 16 actions; this one names 17" and "must be an object of 1 to 64 fields".

Add a `ModuleRegistry::patch_action(id)` that refuses an unknown, non-patch or unavailable action with one wording, and rebuild `validate_settings` as `check_settings` plus `patch_action` plus `check_parameters`, so the shape has one check and `check_settings`'s wording. The shape assertions that change with it are presets/tests.rs ~1039, 1073, 1078, 1092, 1098 and 1179 and presets/library_tests.rs ~290 and 309; capture's own `fields` request ("fields names 1 to 16 actions", library.rs ~534) is a different parameter and keeps its wording. The rule messages ("unknown action X", "X is not a field-patch action", "unavailable module M") are already shared by validation, capture and plans and stay byte-identical; only the Lightroom mapping's report text rewords.

`patch_action` stays independent of source kind and asset: registered, `patch` and available. It keys on `action.patch`, not on the action belonging to a field-patch module, so `set-raw` resolves through it. The source-kind rules stay layered on top at their callers: `check_applies_to` in capture, and in `resolve_plan` the `applies_to` skip (~495) and the `superseded_field` skip (~505-516).

`resolve_plan`'s order stays: an unknown or non-patch step is refused, then a step whose module does not apply to the photo is skipped, and only then is availability checked. A step from an unavailable RAW module on a JPEG photo is therefore reported skipped, not refused.

tasks.description: Generalize the field-patch module's Field and Values to any declared parameter kind, and turn the developer controls proof into a field-patch spec so every field-patch module shares one semantics.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. Tone Curve, the next planned module, needs this to be a spec rather than a third hand-written module.

`field_patch.rs`'s `Field` holds only f64 state (36-62) and `Values` a `Vec<f64>` (253-280) read through `get`, `as_slice` and `all_default`, which `number(name)` and a by-value default check replace; its `read` re-implements the numeric range check `check_value` already provides, and its labels format numbers only. `tests/modules/conformance/shape.rs`'s `Field::read` (29-31) accepts only Number parameters, so a curve, enum or boolean patch module is invisible to the suite.

`modules/controls.rs` (281 lines, the only exerciser of curve, toggle, choice and colour patch controls) hand-writes merge, canonical form, a no-op test by JSON-map equality (so a stored `{"amount":1}` and the bare number `1.0` count as different), and "exactly one field" enforced twice, and it refuses a stored default that equals the field's own declared default.

What field_patch.rs gained for control variants must carry over: `Field.variants` and `Group.reset_variants` are folded onto `Control::number` and the group in `Spec::descriptor` (~165-210), so a non-numeric field with variants needs a build-time rule; `variant_reset` (~458-486) writes `number(field.default)` for every field not superseded; and `whole_group` (~439-450) and its use in `label()` (~631-636) take `(&String, f64)` pairs. The conformance suite mirrors the whole-group label rule in `shape.rs`'s `expected_label`.

`set-raw` is also `patch: true` but is not a field patch: the RAW module merges it itself under the white-balance-in-force rule (modules/raw.rs ~357, 461-500) and keeps that merge. The suite recognizes modules by the field-patch shape, so `set-raw` is outside it; consider having it exercise every `patch: true` action generically so `set-raw` is covered too.

The curve control vocabulary stays even though only the controls proof uses it today; Tone Curve is its planned consumer, so the generalization must leave curve, enum, boolean and colour controls usable by a real module, not only the proof.

Renders stay byte-identical: every numeric module must keep compiling the same f64s through the generalized accessor. A stored-payload refusal's wording may change under current-shapes-only, but the conformance suite's refusal-by-name checks must still pass.

tasks.description: Add a validating Spec constructor for field-patch modules, check group membership at build time, and replace the four hard-coded built-in-module lists with one committed descriptor snapshot.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation.

The same EffectDescriptor literal (format: EFFECT_FORMAT, artifacts: false, single: true, sources: Vec::new()) and templated set/reset ActionText are repeated in basic/mod.rs (123-131), mixer/mod.rs (195-203), presence/mod.rs (80-88) and vignette/mod.rs (88-96). Each also repeats its own neutral short-circuit in compile: basic (:282), mixer (:251) and the vignette (:178) return ColorOperation::neutral() and presence (:144) SpatialOperation::neutral(); the vignette's asks its own is_neutral override (:171-173, an amount of 0) while the others ask all_default. The shared short-circuit therefore asks the module's is_neutral and returns the Color or Spatial neutral by stage.

About 700 lines across those four files' tests exist only to restate the same descriptor table, and Basic's (~429-760) now restate its control variants too. field_patch.rs builds a module's groups with filter_map(|name| self.field(name)) twice, for the sliders (:187) and the group reset's preset (:197), so a misspelled group entry silently produces a field with no slider whose group reset does not reset it, and nothing today catches that.

Separately, registering a built-in module means editing four hard-coded lists: the 18-method literal (~2108-2127) in api/methods.rs's host_and_generated_methods_are_unique_complete_and_match_the_schema test (~2086), registry/tests.rs's action list and descriptors().len() == 9 assertion (:521), xtask/src/editor_acceptance.rs's lists of 9 modules and 18 actions (49-82), and the maskable-effects list in registry/lookups_tests.rs (238-256).

Descriptor JSON must serialize identically before and after; the snapshot this task adds is the proof, and it captures each effect's sources, each control's variants, each parameter's superseded list in schema.list, and module.list's host array beside the modules. A spec must not silently allow single: false, a sources list or another change to the forced fields.

tasks.description: Implement the shared Exposure and White balance control set for JPEG and RAW photos per the source-controls design, on the owner's decisions of 2026-09-27.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation.

The owner took every recommended default of the design on 2026-09-27 (docs/decisions.md, "Source-kind controls"): Exposure is Basic's on every kind, masked white balance on RAW is relative, the JPEG and RAW scales and ranges stay, Lightroom Temperature and Tint import converts through the chromaticity they name, presets store each kind's white balance separately and skip what does not apply, and Reset Basic on RAW also returns the development to As shot.

The host still reads the RAW module's payload directly: editor/source.rs's raw_settings, resolve_raw_settings, development_gains and raw_payload all parse RawPayload, and resolve_raw_settings and development_gains each resolve its white-balance mode to gains with the same As-shot/Custom match, written a third time inside the module itself. Removing exposure from the payload touches these; moving the payload's compilation into the module is not required by this task's acceptance.

TASK-004 is not a prerequisite. set-raw is a `patch: true` action planned by the RAW module itself, because its payload is a development (gains, as-shot gains, calibration) rather than a map of fields, and its merge is the white-balance-in-force rule rather than a field overwrite; `white-balance` uses the existing enum parameter kind. StageContext carries no source kind today, so the RAW module's plan inspects the stack's first layer directly instead of being told the kind; give it one as part of this work.

A query also carries no mask target, so a masked Neutral picker would resolve against the stage before the global Basic layer applies, which is wrong whenever a global white balance exists; the desktop avoids this today only by leaving mask mode before entering Basic's pick mode. Resolve this rather than leaving it latent.

RAW action identities and payload fields are hard-coded in the harness (xtask/src/raw_editor.rs's script steps and control checks, xtask/src/raw_panel_smoke.rs's constants and field lookups); these move to the merged action and its fields with this change.

tasks.description: Build the vignette's per-row and per-column falloff tables lazily on first use instead of in the unit's constructor, and measure owner-thread time per slider tick with a shaped vignette at 60 MP.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed.

modules/vignette/unit.rs's Vignette::new builds two Vec<f64> tables sized width and height (15,840 entries combined at 60 MP, 9504x6336) with a powf call per entry whenever roundness is negative (the superellipse branch), and it runs at every compile, not only at render; vignette/mod.rs's compile constructs a fresh Vignette on every call.

The registry's compile_layers_sampled (modules/registry/compile.rs, which imports render::{Compiled, Entry, Segment, spatial} directly) also runs for callers that need only the output stage: editor/plan.rs's with_stage_context (every plan, draft.set, a composite step and a query), editor/evaluate.rs's analysis_identity (once per preview job), and editor/describe.rs through input_stages.

Suspected cost: roughly +0.1 to +1.5 ms of owner-thread time per slider tick on any module when the stack holds a superellipse vignette (two to three compiles per tick, plus one per preset step), against the draft.set round-trip p50 of about 0.2-0.3 ms recorded in docs/specs/performance.md.
Renders and the vignette's describe and is_finite outputs must stay byte-identical; this is a lazy-build change only, not a change to the falloff arithmetic.

tasks.description: Trim ToolModule to one describe hook in place of three always-together methods, collapse to one history-label mechanism, stop parse re-validating already-declared ranges, and remove the always-unreachable Unavailable forwarding wrapper.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure.

modules/mod.rs's ToolModule trait has 12 methods; settings (what a preset captures, defaulting to values and narrowed by the RAW module) joined with the shared Exposure and White balance controls. describe_layer, values and is_neutral are read together for every row of recipe.describe (editor/describe.rs, is_neutral through registry/compile.rs's layer_neutral), each re-reading the same payload; values is also read alone, by editor/source.rs's superseded-field check and presets/library.rs's capture. Collapsing the three into one describe(...) -> LayerReport, whose values those readers and settings' default take, removes about 60 lines across the 7 production implementations (the field-patch module, presets, RAW, pixel, transform, crop and the capabilities proof), the Unavailable wrapper and about 15 test modules.

Two label mechanisms coexist: label() (implemented by the field-patch module, presets and RAW) and declared summary templates (pixel.rs's "Pixel {x}, {y}", transform.rs's "{transform}" and crop/module.rs's "Crop {angle}°" and "Crop {aspect}", with check_summary, render_summary and action_label in descriptor.rs), combined at one site in editor/plan.rs's action resolution; the desktop never reads summary. module.list publishes summary on every action, so removing it changes the committed descriptor snapshot by that field alone, and docs/user-guide.md's module.list description names summary templates.

parse in crop/module.rs (FitRequest::parse's aspect, aspect-width, aspect-height, angle and centre bounds) and pixel.rs (coordinate_value and color_value) re-checks ranges and enum membership the generic parameter check already enforces. The RAW module's parse is already down to its one cross-field rule (As shot against a temperature or tint); its plan still re-reads gain and the neutral coordinates with "missing" errors the generic check makes unreachable. The Unavailable wrapper in registry/mod.rs forwards all 12 methods, but every host path checks availability before calling one (editor/plan.rs's check_available before parse and in check_askable, registry/lookups.rs's provider lookup, editor/describe.rs's Availability match, layer_neutral through provider(), the capability host), so its forwards exist only to keep that a property of the host's checks, as its own doc comment says.

tasks.description: Delete the prebuilt JSON-descriptor parse path, give each Control variant its own struct so a wrong builder call is a compile error, add EffectDescriptor and ActionDescriptor constructors, and split descriptor.rs by concern.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure.

modules/descriptor.rs is about 2,990 production lines (types and builders, control variants and their resolution, module validation, parameter declaration, check_value and the settings check, labels and the generic check) plus about 2,700 test lines, including one large single test function. ModuleDescriptor::parse, check_raw_control_hints and capabilities::descriptor::check_raw are error-message passes for descriptors arriving as JSON, and no production code calls them: the developer controls proof, their last production caller, is now a field-patch spec built with typed builders like every other module. Their callers are tests that build descriptors from JSON literals: descriptor.rs's and capabilities/descriptor.rs's own tests, modules/presets.rs, registry/compile_tests.rs, artifacts/testing.rs, capabilities/proof_tests.rs, and the desktop's state/testing.rs and state/presets.rs tests.

The Control builder setters (number_style, rail and the like) silently do nothing when called on the wrong variant, for example a number-only setter on a choice control. Field-patch modules reach Control through their spec's typed FieldControl, but the RAW, pixel, transform and crop modules and the mask commands call the builders directly. Literal EffectDescriptor (about 30), ActionDescriptor (about 75) and ParameterDescriptor (about 55) construction sites exist across the workspace, mostly in tests.

AGENTS.md rules out building for external module loading now ("required later, not now"), so deleting the JSON-parse path removes dead generality rather than a used capability. Descriptor JSON must serialize identically before and after, proven by the committed snapshot (fixtures/modules/builtin-descriptors.json, checked by tests/modules/descriptors.rs). The patch-action repository rule also matches a patch action declared in a JSON descriptor; with the parse path gone, its JSON tokens can go too.

The desktop's control mirror (state/tools.rs's Rendered) matches Control's variants; per-variant structs change what it matches, so this lands before, or together with, the desktop change that matches core controls directly.

tasks.description: Register test-only modules, including the always-on pixel proof, only in developer mode, and assemble the built-in registry through one function shared by the desktop and luxforge-json.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure.

The pixel proof's descriptor declares developer: true, but luxforge_core::builtin_modules() (modules/registry/mod.rs) always includes it, so its PointReplace primitive, its pixel stage and about 150 render lines stay live, and edit.set-pixel is on every production API and in the committed descriptor snapshot of ModuleRegistry::builtin(). The controls proof, by contrast, is added by luxforge-app's app/lifecycle.rs registry() only in developer mode (automatic in debug builds, --developer in optimized ones).

luxforge-cli/src/json.rs assembles its own registry from ModuleRegistry::builtin() plus the capabilities proof whenever --proof-endpoint is given, and has no developer switch, so the desktop and the JSON CLI already differ: the desktop serves the capability proof only with --developer --proof-endpoint, luxforge-json with --proof-endpoint alone.

Many tests reach the pixel proof through ModuleRegistry::builtin(): core unit and integration tests (the owner, preview, export and mask tests among them), luxforge-app's tests/json_cli.rs, and xtask's histogram scenario (which commits edit.set-pixel in the real editor), controls scenario, editor-acceptance and the Basic and mask acceptance chapters. Each moves to a developer registry or a developer launch; an evidence launch passes --developer only through the scenario launch envelope (xtask/src/scenario/launch.rs), as the editor-launch repository rule requires.

The desktop group's move of the headless luxforge-json binary into its own crate without the GUI stack means the one assembly function belongs where both binaries can reach it (luxforge-core, or a crate both depend on), not in luxforge-app.

Owner decision: test modules, including the pixel proof, register only in developer mode. PointReplace's own fate (seed the eventual repair primitive, or deletion) is decided separately alongside the repair-stage design; this task only stops registering it by default.

Owner decision (2026-09-28, docs/decisions.md "Plan refresh"): luxforge-json takes the desktop's --developer flag with the same meaning and refuses --proof-endpoint without it, as the desktop does, but is not put in developer mode automatically in debug builds; process tests and harness runs that need a test module pass --developer.

Developer mode must keep every developer-only module unchanged; outside it, schema.list must drop every developer-only method, and the committed descriptor snapshot (of the normal registry) loses the pixel proof's entries.

tasks.description: Delete the per-module copies of sample-equals-render, the host-journey re-run, neutral-compiles-to-nothing and compile-refusal checks that the shape-driven conformance suite now proves generically, naming each deleted assertion's keeper.
extra_context: Wave 5, tests.

Per-module copies of host-level checks remain after the registry-driven conformance suite (tests/modules/conformance: sample_equals_render, renders_nothing and stored_refusals in pixels.rs, the rules in rules.rs, the journey in journey.rs) took them over: sample-equals-render in tests/basic/{exposure,white_balance,tone,colour}.rs, tests/modules/{mixer,presence}.rs and xtask/src/basic_acceptance.rs's render.sample probe; the host journey re-run in tests/basic/exposure.rs (the_first_set_places_one_layer_before_the_geometry_tail_and_later_sets_update_it); "neutral compiles to nothing" in modules/basic/mod.rs (compilation_produces_an_exposure_unit_a_tone_unit_both_or_neither), modules/mixer/mod.rs and modules/presence/mod.rs (compile_is_neutral_for_the_empty_payload_...), modules/vignette/mod.rs (compile_of_a_zero_amount_payload_is_the_neutral_colour_operation) and presence/oracle.rs (every_unit_at_zero_is_omitted_and_the_neutral_payload_compiles_to_nothing); and the discovery steps of tests/basic/white_balance.rs's picker journey. The vignette's own discovery test went with the descriptor snapshot.

The per-module Presence sampling alone is the most expensive part of the modules test binary: tests/modules/presence.rs's production_matches_the_reference_through_both_render_paths runs 2 images times 4 parameter sets times 1,280 pixels times 2 render paths, about 26 million pixel evaluations, to prove what the render-level spatial suite already proves with cheap units.

Keep each module's numerics against its own frozen corpus, its history-word tests, its placement test and any genuinely module-specific behavior. Add the field-order assertions the deleted per-module tests incidentally provided for the mixer and vignette (one describe-based assertion each), so a field-order swap is still caught. A commit that deletes a test names, for each assertion, the kept test that proves the same fact.

basic_acceptance.rs's probe is also in scope of the harness group's narrowing of editor-acceptance, whose owner decision keeps Basic's numerics on the photo fixture against the independent reference there; whichever change lands first removes the probe and the other drops it from its list.

The private sRGB transfer-function copies in test code are already gone: the harness group's one sRGB reference replaced them with luxforge-reference's one set of functions, and the srgb-transfer-function repository rule keeps it single.

tasks.description: Give ToolModule a defaulted carry hook so a later geometry module is repositioned by the orientation the way the crop is today, instead of transform.rs naming the crop directly.
extra_context: Wave 6, roadmap groundwork.
Blocked: starts when the first new geometry module (for example upright or perspective) is designed.

modules/transform.rs imports crop::stored_payload and CROP_EFFECT directly and re-expresses only the crop through a turn, via CropPayload's carried method in modules/crop/geometry.rs: the one place a module reads and rewrites another module's stored payload (Basic's spec also takes the RAW module's white-balance control variants, but those are declared controls, not a payload). A second geometry effect placed after the orientation (an upright or perspective module, say) would keep its stored payload unchanged while its input stage turns, so it would silently address different image content; nothing today refuses this.

Non-affine geometry is out of scope for the hook itself: it would need a new host primitive through processing.rs, registry/compile.rs's output_stage, the point walk (render/pipeline.rs's Evaluation::entry_pixel), the byte driver and locate (render.rs), render/linear.rs and render/window.rs, wherever the render.rs split puts them. Record that in docs/design/architecture.md so a future module does not fake one through the carry hook.
